summary: The root طود (Twd) primarily refers to a great mountain, especially one that rises high into the sky. It can also describe an elevated tract of sand.
lane: طَوْدٌ ذ A mountain: (K:) or a great mountain (S, A, L, K) rising high into the sky: (A:) or i. q. هَضْبَةٌ [either as denoting a hill or mountain or a tract of sand: see the next sentence]: (IAar:) pl. أَطْوَادٌ (A, L, K) and طِوَدَةٌ . (K.) -b2- And An elevated, or overlooking, tract of sand; (K, TA;) as also هَضْبَةٌ . (TA.) -b3- And the pl. أَطْوَاد is applied by a poet to signify (tropical:) Camels' humps; as being likened to mountains because of their height. (IAar, L.) -b4- اِبْنُ الطَّوْدِ means (assumed tropical:) The mass of rock ( الجُلْمُودُ ) that falls from the upper part of a mountain: (A, L, * K: *) or the echo. (A.) One says, أَسْرَعُ مِنِ ٱبْنِ الطَّوْدِ (assumed tropical:) Quicker, or swifter, than the mass of rock that falls &c.: or than the echo. (A.)
